notation.purpose: Condensed moves, replies, and saved positions; never general headings.

motion.name: hint
motion.purpose: Draw the hint arrow from stroke-dashoffset 100 to 0.

motion.name: piece-move
motion.purpose: Glide an adjacent legal move or undo, including the castling rook. Skip for loading, position jumps, flips, and reduced motion.

motion.name: analysis
motion.purpose: Move the analysis indicator from translateX(0) to translateX(240%).

motion.name: journey-marker
motion.purpose: Show hover and selection on connected journey markers.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: none !important; transition: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important
motion.purpose: Applied to all elements and pseudo-elements when reduced motion is requested.

components.name: Primary button
components.description: The visible next decision: Show hint, Play followed by move notation, or the current practice action.

components.name: Coaching modes
components.description: Three explicit coaching times: before a mistake, after a mistake, or after the game.

components.name: Move choice
components.description: A selectable chess move that controls the board arrow. Phone choices use a 40px minimum height; Play and Why? share the action row below.

components.name: Decision coach
components.description: A compact cue and visible decisions beside the board, or below it on phones. Longer explanations open in a dialog. Completed games with a turning point make Practice this primary. Personal practice keeps answers hidden until help is requested, shows Try again and See the reply for an incorrect move, and distinguishes first-attempt solutions without help from assisted solutions. Next position becomes Finish practice on the last position; completion shows solved and independent counts with one primary Back to game action. Show hint is prominent before help; selected hints show Play with move notation and Why?. Concrete warnings offer Show a move, Play anyway, and Pause warnings. The first engine recommendation is not warned against. Ask Rook is removed; threat checks use the explanation dialog. Authored lessons show one short task, one progress bar per player move, scripted replies, and a retry after an incorrect move. Completion distinguishes assisted and independent runs. Next lesson is primary; Try without hints repeats, and Play from here is available only on nonterminal boards.

components.name: Dialog surface
components.description: A focused surface for secondary tasks, move explanations, threat checks, and full game review. Its header stays visible while content scrolls. Practice selection and saved positions open here; personal practice runs on the main board. Saved rows keep the original move and answer behind What happened? and show independent, assisted, or ready-to-practice status. Game, lesson, report, panel, and selected journey views have revisitable hash URLs; hint URLs retain the exact legal UCI move. Account identifiers and private learning records stay out of URLs. The skill-filtered picker contains three openings and 22 challenges in separate compact row groups. Its select and count wrap on narrow screens. Each lesson has a stable learn or practice URL, and the picker retains its selected skill in the URL. New game and Start over open this surface before replacing the board. The lesson confirmation includes Start over with the current lesson title. Keep playing, close, and Escape cancel. The notice confirms that learning progress and saved positions stay.
components.html:
Your game

Practice and saved positions open here.

components.name: Board destinations
components.description: Blue and cool white squares with original white and navy Staunton pieces, gold state overlays, deep navy legal destinations, and a dark blue hint arrow. A small board-state sample. In play, the shell fills 100dvh under a 56px header (48px on phones). ResizeObserver fits the board to the width and height left by controls and the guide, capped at 720px. Phones stack the guide below; short landscape windows use two columns. Personal practice uses this same board for up to three distinct saved positions, with progress in the opponent strip and reply controls after an incorrect move. Back to game restores the original game while retaining practice evidence. Refresh reopens the active URL position as practice, with Back to game preserving the saved original game. New game remains visible above free play; Start over appears above an authored lesson. Both open the confirmation dialog before the board changes. Personal practice shows its position count in that space.

components.name: Connected journey
components.description: Six available places connected by dashed paths and selected jade paths. Saved practice and authored lesson results establish exploration. Each selected detail shows a short cue, completed lessons out of the matching curriculum, and independent lesson completions. Explore lessons is primary; Revisit my positions is a secondary text action when saved positions exist. Independent evidence uses an ink check on jade. Selection has its own hash URL. Wide maps use two rows and three columns; narrow maps use three rows and two columns. Short landscape places the detail beside the map. At widths up to 600px and heights up to 620px, the dialog height is calc(100dvh - 16px), with 8px header top and body bottom padding.

narrative.overview:
Nextmove uses a quiet, late-night strategy-game frame. Charcoal surfaces surround blue and cool white squares, original white and navy Staunton pieces, and gold move marks. The board carries the action; short, plain coaching appears when a decision needs support.

The interface uses code, SVG pieces, and line icons. It has no raster texture or decorative image layer. Type, color, and motion help the player read the next move.
keyCharacteristics: A large, clear board within a quiet charcoal frame.
Jade actions and warm warning states.
DM Sans cues with condensed chess notation.
Small control groups and explanations that open on request.

rules.name: The State Rule
rules.body: Use color to reinforce a visible state, not as its only signal.

rules.name: The Plain Cue Rule
rules.body: Keep coaching in sentence case and plain type. Reserve condensed type for chess notation.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: Keep the board, guide, and main controls visible without page scrolling. Resize the board to fit the available space; do not clip page overflow to hide controls. Pause actions appear once in the guide, with no duplicate sticky action row.

dos: Do keep the board, pieces, destinations, and hint arrow clear at phone size.
Do use jade for actions and current state, with labels or shapes for meaning.
Do keep the coach concise and put longer move explanations and threat checks in dialogs.
Do fit the board, guide, and main controls in one window without page scrolling.
Do preserve keyboard focus, accessible labels, and reduced-motion support.
donts: Don't restore the old olive, acid-yellow, grain, or tilted-mark identity.
Don't add a welcome hero, slogans, or a permanent lesson dashboard to play.
Don't use condensed type for headings or teaching prose.
Don't rely on color alone to explain legal moves, check, or selection.
